statements.venue: Letter to Anysphere from Chairmen Garbarino (Homeland Security) and Moolenaar (Select Committee on China), quoted in committee press release
statements.quote: guardrails designed to prevent their models from being used to develop weapons, automate software vulnerability discovery and exploitation, generate tailored disinformation, or assist in the synthesis of dangerous chemical or biological agents
statements.context: Joint investigation into Chinese AI models built by distilling American frontier models and stripping out their safeguards, which the letter warns may then reach hostile states, terrorists and criminals.

statements.reason: The letter names AI helping to make chemical or biological agents, but only as misuse by hostile states, terrorists and criminals, so ruling 1 makes it C; it sits near D because the danger is described through the guardrails labs build.

grade_reason: His strongest 2026 statement is a co-signed letter naming AI-assisted synthesis of chemical or biological agents, which is misuse only and therefore C. His own remarks are about cyber threats (D), and he said he does not think we should slow down, which is a policy view, not a dismissal.
notes: All seven web searches in this run ran (the six required plus one on the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act).
